newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian cen bank governor sees EMU on time - paper.
newsitem.headline: Belgian cen bank governor sees EMU on time - paper.

text.p: National Bank of Belgium Governor Alfons Verplaetse expects Europe's single currency to start on time in 1999, La Libre Belgique newspaper quoted him as saying in an interview published on Wednesday.

"Certainly the events of the past six weeks were not foreseen. (But) they only show the march toward a single currency is irreversible even if there are sometimes small hiccups. (The) Amsterdam (summit) has called nothing into question," Verplaetse said.

Verplaetse said he believed France had won something by getting European Union leaders to coordinate employment policies. But said those who believed tweeking the demand side of the economy was the right way to create jobs were wrong.
Verplaetse said he also supported the French idea of an economic government to coordinate contacts with the planned European Central Bank.
"It is not necessary but perhaps useful. There are certain areas where there needs to be an exchange of views between the ECB and governments," Verplaetse said.
He added, however, he was against any infringement of the ECB's independent status.
